label: text
text: The Committee on the composition of the League Council has adopted the Drafting Sub-Committee's modified scheme.

label: text
text: The Spanish member did not vote.

label: text
text: The Polish member declared his "partial abstention."

label: text
text: The Committee on the composition of the League Council commenced the discussion on the question of permanent seats.

label: text
text: Senor Palacios (Spain) upheld Spain's claim for a permanent seat.

label: text
text: M. Fromagcot, (France) hoped that Spain would reconsider her decision.

label: text
text: Herr von Hoesch (Germany) expressed the sincere desire of Germany for continued co-operation with Spain in the League. He was of opinion that the matter should be left to the decision of the assembly.

label: text
text: M. Brouckere (Belgium) strongly opposed an increase in the number of permanent seats. He ardently hoped for the continuation of Spain in the work of the League, and regarded that this would be attained by the scheme now adopted.

label: text
text:
Japan had always been in favour of Spain's requests, though unfortunately circumstances prevented its realization. The Japanese Government hoped that Spain would consider carefully the draft regulations which had been adopted.
Mr. Chu (China) hoped that the Committee would reconsider the question of permanent seats, increase their number correspondingly, and decrease the non-permanent seats. He said that China would claim a permanent seat in the event of more being created at any time beyond Germany's.
Signor Scialoja (Italy) regretted that they were unable to satisfy Spain's claim. He hoped that after hearing the report of the Committee's discussions, the Spanish Government would reconsider its attitude and continue to co-operate in the League.
M. Sioborg (Sweden) and Senor

label: text
text: M. Sjoborg (Sweden) and Senor Guani (Uruguay) spoke in the same strain.

label: text
text: In the course of his speech Count Sato (Japan) expressed sympathy with China's claim for a permanent sent. "China is our great neighbour and country with which we naturally desire the best relations. Her claim ought to be considered in conformity with the principle of geographical position."—Réuter.

label: text
text: According to "Le Petit Parisien" M. Briand, the French Minister for Foreign Affairs, and Sir Auston Chamberlain, the British Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, at their meeting last night realised the similarity of their dispositions with regard to the French and British Cabinets concerning Tangier and the seats on the Council of the League of Nations.

label: text
text: Both statesmen decided to cooperate closely and not to allow the work of the League to be affected or permit the question of Tanglers to be discussed by other Powers than those interested. —Router.

label: text
text: The Foreign Minister, Senior Yangua, in a speech with reference to the League Assembly, said that Spain resolutely maintained her demand for a permanent seat on the Council and was in no way interested in other formulae—leuter.

label: text
text:
M. Motta (Switzerland), Chairman of the Committee considering the composition of the Council, stated definitely that it is understood that Germany will have a permanent seat.
The Spanish delegate is referring the matter to Madrid. Meanwhile he requests the Committee frame majority and minority reports with mention of the Spanish claim for a permanent seat.
Reuter.

text: The returns of over half the divisions in the California Republican primary elections show that Lieut-Governor Young is ahead of Mr. F. William Richardson, the incumbent for the Governorship, by 22,000 votes.

label: text
text: Lieut-Governor Young adheres to President Coolidge's policies, including the World Court at The Hague.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Lieutenant Cyrus Bettla, winner of the Pulitzer air race in 1925, has died in hospital as the result of a crash.—-Reuter.

label: text
text: The French aviators Challe and Werzer have arrived at Bander Abbas (Persck) on a non-stop run from Paris, beating the world record for a non-stop flight held by the Frenchman, Lieut. Grier, from Paris to Omsk.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The Special Commission of the League of Nations appointed to consider the composition of the League Council to-day completed its examination of the question of distribution of non-permanent seats on the Council.

label: text
text: The final draft decisions, which were approved by the Commission—the Spanish representative alone abstaining—incorporate in "the "Cecil" plan the modifications which have been closely discussed by the Sub-Committee for the past two days. In the form in which they will be presented to the League Council for approval the main features of Lord Cecil's plan are retained.

label: text
text: The Council will be increased in size by the addition of three non-permanent members. All the non-permanent members will normally be elected for three years, and one-third will be elected annually. The scheme provides that the Assembly may endow three of the occupants of these seats with semi-permanence by declaring them re-eligible for election for a further period of three years, after having already served for that length of time.

label: text
text: The discussion has for the most part ranged around the immediate method of election that should be adopted. The proposals now drafted, which it is taken for granted will be approved by the Council, provide that the Assembly shall decide which of the nine members elected for this year shall sit for one, which for two, and which for three years. The Assembly may also decide at the 1926 election, by special two-thirds majorities vote in each case that not more than three of the members elected shall be re-eligible. The designation of these three members, however, would not deprive the Assembly of its right, which is asserted in an earlier article of the draft, to designate as re-eligible any member or members retiring from a non-permanent seat next year or in 1928, but it would be understood that only in exceptional circumstances would this right be exercised.

label: text
text:
The proposals are regarded here as a good compromise between the conflicting views and at the same time as calculated to meet the aspiration of those members who have claimed permanent seats.
The special Commission is engaged in considering what changes, if any, should be made in regard to permanent seats on the Council—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text:
Seventeen persons were killed and 36 wounded as the result of the derailment of a mail train running from Barcelona to Valencia, near Tortosa, in consequence of a landslip following heavy rain. A third class carriage was telescoped. Several villages in the environs of Barcelona are infundated by rains. Thirty-six persons have perished in the floods, and great material damage has been caused.
—Reuter.

label: text
text: At least 24 persons were killed and 50 injured in the Tortosa disaster.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Optimistic communiques from Hankow continue to arrive, claiming the recovery of Puchi and the advance of the Northerners towards the Hupeh-Hunan border.

label: text
text: Independent reports do not confirm the Northern successes, but none of the reports mentions any further advance of the Southerners. There seems no doubt that heavy fighting is proceeding and that Wu Pei-fu is receiving large reinforcements from the North.—Reuter.

label: text
text: According to Japanese reports from Hankow Wu Pei-fu's forces are demoralised and have suffered several reverses. The Southerners are advancing rapidly against Wuchang, which is across the river from Hankow. The reports add that Wu Pei-fu's forces are preparing to check the "Red" advance at Chihfangshih, twelve miles from Wuchang, and are also constructing trenches at the suburbs of Wuchang.

label: text
text: The Northern reinforcements continue to arrive in large numbers at Hankow Refugees from Wuchang and the surrounding districts are pouring in to the Hankow Concessions.

label: text
text: Sun Chuan-fang, so far, has sent merely a handful of troops to assist Wu Pei-fu, and it is believed that Sun intends to maintain armei neutrality unless his five provinces are invaded; but he is enrolling recruits and taking all precautions. —Reuter.

label: text
text:
This morning a Chinese foreman, employed at the Ewo Cotton Mills, was waylaid at a wayside road in the eastern district of the city by a gang of armed men, who mortally injured him with six bullets. The foreman, before his death, was unable to make a statement identifying the assailants, who, so far, have not been arrested.
Meantime, a meeting of the Strike Pickets' Committee has authorised the pickets to resort to the use of axes, iron bars and arms in the case of a clash with mill operatives desiring to go to work or with the police, promising compensation in the event of injury or of the death of picketers.
—Reuter.

label: text
text: The Governor of the Island of Horta, in the Azores, now cables that eight persons were killed and 200 injured in the Fayal earthquake. Four hundred houses were razed at Flamangas, in a continuous series of short shocks.

label: text
text: The Government has ordered the immediate departure of two cruisers and a transport vessel with medical units and a detachment of engineers.—Reuter.

label: text
text:
The Governor of Horta cabled that there were fifty casualties (killed and injured combined) as a result of the earthquake.—Rutur.
RUTH ST. DENIS, TED SHAWN
